# ROOTS-AI™ — governed narrative settings

Prepared in response to the ROOTS review of 29 September 2026, item B3.

**Generated by** `npm run evidence:ai-settings`. Every value in the *Local* column is read from
the running configuration, not transcribed, so this table cannot drift from what the code does.

## Why the production column is empty

The production values live in the Cloudflare Worker's environment. **We do not read that
environment**, and filling the column from memory or inference would produce a table that looks
authoritative and is not — which is exactly how the misnamed key went unnoticed in the first
place.

So the column is left for whoever holds that console, with the check to run beside each row. The
checks are written so that each can be confirmed from a generated report or a test, without
needing to read a secret.

**One thing worth doing first.** A Workers deploy replaces the whole `vars` set, so a value
edited only in the dashboard is lost at the next deploy. Anything set there should also be in
`wrangler.jsonc`, or kept as a secret, which deploys do not touch.

## Settings

| Setting | Where | Local | Production | What it governs | How to check it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AI_NARRATIVE_ENABLED` | Environment | **not set** — narrative off | | AI-11 kill switch. Anything but the exact string `true` means off, and every governed section falls back to its approved deterministic copy. | A report generated with it off carries `outcome: deterministic_fallback` and `fallback_reason: not_configured`. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Environment (secret) | **not set** | | Provider credential. Absent or misnamed, every report falls back — silently, until the provenance is read. | A generated report shows `outcome: generated`. `not_configured` means the key was never read, which is what a misnamed secret looks like. |
| `OPENAI_MODEL` | Environment | **not set** — defaults to `gpt-4.1` | | AI-11. ROOTS can change the approved model without a code change. Whatever is used is recorded on the report (AI-06). | The `model` field in the report's narrative provenance matches the value set. |
| `PROVIDER` | Code constant | `openai` | | OPS-06: no new provider without ROOTS approval. Changing it is a code change and a ROOTS decision, which is why it is not an environment variable. | Recorded in every report's provenance. |
| `DEFAULT_MODEL` | Code constant | `gpt-4.1` | | Used when `OPENAI_MODEL` is unset. The approved model of record. | Compare with the provenance on a report generated with no `OPENAI_MODEL` set. |
| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | Code constant | 20000 ms | | AI-07 — per attempt, so the participant never waits indefinitely. §12 requires a governed fallback on provider timeout. | `tests/ai/outcomes.test.ts`, the timeout case: the report falls back with `fallback_reason: timeout`. |
| `MAX_ATTEMPTS` | Code constant | 2 | | AI-07 retry. Worst case a participant waits 2 × 20 s = 40 s before the deterministic report is produced. | `tests/ai/outcomes.test.ts`: one retry then acceptance, and a provider error on every attempt stopping after exactly this many. |
| `temperature` | Provider request | `0.3` | | Low: the narrative describes a fixed, already-calculated result, so variation adds nothing and costs reproducibility. | Read from `lib/ai/provider.ts` at generation time. |
| `max_tokens` | Provider request | `900` | | Bounds the response. The C-03 §4.2 word limits are enforced separately by the schema check, which rejects an over-long narrative rather than truncating it. | `tests/ai/boundary.test.ts` — word limits. |
| `response_format` | Provider request | `{ type: 'json_object' }` | | The response must be JSON for the schema check to run at all. A model that does not support this mode returns prose and every report falls back with `invalid_json`. | `tests/ai/outcomes.test.ts`, the invalid-JSON case. |
| `store` | Provider request | `false` | | False: the provider is asked not to retain the request. The projection holds no answers and no identity, but retention is still declined. | Read from `lib/ai/provider.ts`; confirm against the provider account's own retention setting. |
| `PROMPT_VERSION` | Code constant | `1.0.0` | | AI-06 — recorded on every report so a narrative can be traced to the prompt that produced it. | Present in the report's narrative provenance. |
| `SCHEMA_VERSION` | Code constant | `1.0.0` | | AI-06. The schema a narrative was accepted against. | Present in the provenance. |
| `CONTENT_LIBRARY_VERSION` | Code constant | `C-03-v1.0.1` | | AI-04 — the approved content the narrative is grounded in. | Present in the provenance. |
| `FALLBACK_VERSION` | Code constant | `1.0.0-deterministic-fallback` | | C-03 §7 — the approved deterministic copy used when no narrative is accepted. | Present in the provenance, and carried in the report's narrative template version. |

## What the report records, whatever happens

Every report carries its narrative provenance, whether a narrative was used or not. That is what
makes this table checkable after the fact rather than only at deploy time:

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-4.1",
  "prompt_version": "1.0.0",
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "content_library_version": "C-03-v1.0.1",
  "fallback_version": "1.0.0-deterministic-fallback",
  "outcome": "generated | generated_after_retry | deterministic_fallback",
  "fallback_reason": "not_configured | timeout | provider_error | invalid_json | schema_rejected | prohibited_language"
}
```

`fallback_reason` is the field that matters operationally. `not_configured` means the key was
never read — a missing or misnamed secret. `provider_error` means the provider was reached and
refused. The two look identical to a participant and are completely different to fix, which is
why they are recorded separately.

## Scope, stated because a settings table invites the question

None of these settings can affect a score. The narrative may replace three sections of the
report (2, 9 and 18) and nothing else; it is given a projection of values already calculated,
never answers; and it holds no database credential of any kind. Turning it off changes what
those three sections say and changes no number in the report.

That boundary is asserted by `tests/ai/boundary.test.ts` and, in the database, by the
`roots_ai_narrative` role's grants, probed by `npm run db:probes`.
